summary: Frontend-only responsive verification of the Hero <picture> switch on Atlas Freight marketing site. Validated across 6 viewports (375, 360, 390, 768 mobile; 1024, 1440 desktop). All checks PASSED: mobile/tablet-portrait viewports load the Indian ornate truck image (photo-1635774152029) with the truck clearly visible and not cropped, while desktop-class viewports (>=1024px) preserve the untouched Scania cinematic close-up (photo-1601584115197). Hero content (trust chip, headline, CTAs) is readable on all mobile sizes. 5-item stats card renders correctly in 2-col mobile layout. Mobile hamburger opens a full-screen opaque drawer with all 6 nav items + GET FREE QUOTE + Chat on WhatsApp + phone + address. Zero console/page errors.

issues: Headline 'Logistics Partner' second line gets slightly clipped at the bottom on very small screens because parallax + gradient overlays it; the word 'Partner' has descender area cut by the overlay/stats card. Not part of current bug scope but worth polishing.

critical_code_review_comments: Hero.jsx <picture> correctly uses media='(min-width: 1024px)' so viewports <1024 (including iPad Mini 768) get the mobile Indian-truck image as required by the spec.
Individual STAT items in the floating card do not carry data-testid (e.g., stat-years-experience). Adding them would improve automated testability but is not a blocker.
Desktop hero image URL (photo-1601584115197) remains unchanged — user's directive respected.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Hero <picture> switch verified working at breakpoints 360/375/390/768 (mobile Indian truck) and 1024/1440 (desktop Scania). Any regression should first re-check img.currentSrc via JS: `document.querySelector('[data-testid="hero-image"]').currentSrc` — expect photo-1635774152029 for <1024px and photo-1601584115197 for >=1024px.
